---
title: "Serving Worker republication"
description: "How production promotion republishes the Workers that already serve roadmap, learn, teach, nova, tools and lms, and how to stop, retry or roll one back."
updatedAt: '2026-11-21'
audience: developers
---

Some native Workers already serve production traffic through the apex gateway
mount and their own hosts. A production promotion must reach them as well, or a
dependency fix (for example a React Server Components advisory) stays merged but
unshipped. `serving-workers-production.yaml` closes that gap.

| App | Worker | Public origins | Sealed artifact |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| roadmap | `tuturuuu-roadmap` | `tuturuuu.com/roadmap` | `roadmap-worker-<sha>` |
| learn | `tuturuuu-learn` | `learn.tuturuuu.com`, `tuturuuu.com/learn` | `learn-cutover-production-<sha>` |
| teach | `tuturuuu-teach` | `teach.tuturuuu.com`, `tuturuuu.com/teach` | `teach-cutover-production-<sha>` |
| nova | `tuturuuu-nova` | `tuturuuu.com/nova` | `nova-cutover-production-<sha>` |
| tools | `tuturuuu-tools` | `tools.tuturuuu.com`, `tuturuuu.com/tools` | `tools-cutover-<sha>` |
| lms | `tuturuuu-lms` | `tuturuuu.com/lms` | `lms-worker-<sha>` |

`scripts/ci/serving-workers-apps.mjs` holds this table. Each app also needs an
`admitted` entry in `productionPublicationPolicy` (`tuturuuu.ci.ts`); a `held`
entry or a `productionAppExclusions` line keeps `plan` from selecting that app
and stops the publisher.

## Flow

On every push to `production`:

1. `plan` runs in the `cloudflare-release-production` environment (production
   branch only). Without the `SERVING_WORKERS_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` secret it
   selects nothing. Otherwise it reads each app's public `/api/build-info` and
   selects every app that does not serve the production SHA yet, so a failed or
   skipped earlier promotion is retried by the next one.
2. Each selected app's own workflow runs through `workflow_call` at the exact
   production SHA and seals its production artifact. Its qualification-only
   `native` jobs do not run on the production ref.
3. `serving-worker-publish.yaml` runs one app at a time per
   `serving-worker-publish-<app>` concurrency group. It restores the sealed
   archive, reruns the seal verifier and converts the archive's own emitted
   config to cf Build Output with `void-cf-output.mjs`. Cron triggers stay
   configured on the Worker and are never part of a version, so they are left
   out of the uploaded config and checked against the live schedules instead.
4. The publisher refuses a split deployment (another rollout is in progress)
   and any source that is not a fast-forward of the live build, and skips when
   live already serves the SHA.
5. `void-cf-publisher.mjs publish --strict` uploads one version with no traffic
   and rejects any binding that differs from the serving version.
6. The candidate is staged at 0% beside the serving version and smoked through
   the `Cloudflare-Workers-Version-Overrides` header, including through the
   apex gateway mount, once the override reaches the candidate (deployment
   writes take a few seconds to propagate). Build-info must report the SHA on every origin, each
   probe must match the serving status and redirect, and the page's scripts and
   stylesheets must return 200. Afterwards the serving version is restored
   alone and must read back steadily, so nothing changes for readers yet.
7. `void-cf-publisher.mjs assign --expect-current <serving>` moves 100% of
   traffic only while the captured version still serves, then waits for the
   public build-info to report the SHA. On failure the captured version is
   restored, but only over a deployment this run wrote; another writer's
   deployment is left in place and recorded.

Every step lands in the `serving-<app>-publication-<sha>-<run>-<attempt>`
artifact, retained 90 days, including the `rollbackVersion` that served before.

## Stop, retry and roll back

- **Stop.** Set the repository variable `SERVING_WORKERS_PUBLICATION` to
  anything other than `enabled`. New runs build and publish nothing. A job reads
  the variable when it starts, so cancel the workflow run to stop a publisher
  that is already running. Cancelling leaves the current step as it is, which
  can be a 0% stage or a just-assigned candidate; restore the receipt's
  `rollbackVersion` as described below.
- **Retry one app.** Dispatch `serving-workers-production.yaml` on `production`
  with that app. It rebuilds only if the app does not serve the SHA yet.
- **Roll back.** Read `rollbackVersion` from the receipt and run
  `cf workers deployments create --worker <worker> --strategy percentage --versions '[{"version_id":"<rollbackVersion>","percentage":100}]'`.
  Routes, custom domains, schedules and the gateway are never changed by this
  flow.

## Activation

Every enabled run publishes each admitted app whose live build differs from
the pinned production SHA, so any regression in that SHA ships with it. Before
setting `SERVING_WORKERS_PUBLICATION=enabled`, confirm the pinned production SHA
has no known regression for an admitted app, for example by smoking each app's
candidate from that SHA at 0%. While a pinned production SHA carries a known
regression, keep the variable unset or move that app to `held` in
`productionPublicationPolicy` until a fixed SHA is pinned.

## Credentials

`SERVING_WORKERS_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` is an environment secret on
`cloudflare-release-production`, scoped to Workers Scripts edit on the
production account only, with no zone permissions. `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and
`NOVA_ABUSE_GUARD_FAMILIES` are repository variables. Rotate the token through
the token ledger and set it with `gh secret set --env` from standard input so it
is never printed.

## Local release

When CI runners are unavailable, mirror the app's own artifact job on a trusted
host at the production SHA, pack the archive the same way, then run the same
publisher with the same environment:

```bash
node scripts/ci/serving-workers.mjs restore <app> <sha> <artifact-dir> <absent-output-dir>
SERVING_WORKERS_PUBLICATION=enabled node scripts/ci/serving-workers.mjs publish <app> <sha> <output-dir>
```

The roadmap seal and its verifier need Linux `/proc`; on macOS run them in a
Linux container, and pack archives with `COPYFILE_DISABLE=1` so macOS metadata
files do not enter the sealed tree. A shallow checkout drops the roadmap commit
metrics, so build roadmap from full history.
